description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” illustrates the number of conversations categorized by topic and whether the recipient was deceived, with data grouped by four categories: “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding” (partially obscured), and “Journalism.” The x-axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” scaled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10, while the y-axis lists the conversation topics. A legend in the upper right corner indicates that red bars correspond to “Deceived: Yes,” yellow to “Deceived: Partially,” and green to “Deceived: No.” For “Academic Collaboration,” approximately 36 conversations resulted in deception (“Yes”), 27 were partially deceived, and 7 were not deceived. In “Recruitment,” about 38 were deceived, 24 partially deceived, and 6 not deceived. For “Academic Funding,” roughly 65 conversations were deceived, 4 partially deceived, and 3 not deceived. In “Journalism,” approximately 15 were deceived, 48 partially deceived, and 6 not deceived. The chart visually emphasizes that “Academic Funding” had the highest number of deceived conversations, while “Journalism” had the highest number of partially deceived conversations. All bars are presented side-by-side per category, with no stacking, allowing direct comparison of deception levels across topics.
